title: The job classes that receive most of the other pay
question: Which job classes receive the most pay outside salary and overtime, in total and for each holder?
finding: Ten job classes received 52% of all other pay in fiscal 2026. The largest is Police Officer 3 (class Q004): $27.1 million for 1,144 holders, $23,654 each and 17.2% of their salary (it was 6.2% in fiscal 2017). Then Registered Nurse (class 2320) ($26.5 million) and Firefighter (class H002) ($21.3 million). For each holder the largest among classes with five or more is Director (class 1115), $162,844 each, followed by Asst Chf of Dept (Fire Dept) (class H050) ($61,205) and Battalion Chief, Fire Suppress (class H040) ($59,458).
how: City payroll file, fiscal 2026 with fiscal 2017 for comparison. Other pay is added up by job class across everyone paid regular salary in the class; board seats, elected offices and the Superior Court are left out. Ranked by money. Classes where other pay is more than a fifth of salary, with the number of years above that line, are listed under City jobs (“Classes where other pay is more than a fifth of salary”) and are not repeated here. Titles are printed as the payroll prints them (Dep is deputy, Chf is chief, Asst is assistant, Sprv is supervisor, Ofc is officer, EMT is emergency medical technician).
limits: The largest classes lead for their size: thousands of nurses, police officers, firefighters and transit operators earn premiums of the kinds their labour agreements set (the agreements are not on disk). A high figure for each holder in a small senior class is more often a payout of unused leave to one or two people who left. The public file does not separate the kinds of payment.
